figure: FIGURE A.1 — Extreme sparsity: single-digit active (2026)
severity: P1 (major; numerically wrong in the headline figure of Appendix A)
issue: The Kimi K3 bar is labelled 3.7% but its own annotation reads "280B/104B active", which is 104/280 = 37.1% — a factor-of-ten discrepancy. The bar length (drawn to ~3.7 on a 0–10 axis) matches the label, so the drawing and the label agree with each other and disagree with the annotation. Two mutually exclusive readings exist: (a) the fraction is wrong and should be ~37.1% (in which case the axis maximum of 10, the bar length, the figure title, and the caption are all wrong); or (b) the annotation is wrong and the denominator is 2.8T (104/2800 = 3.71%, which reproduces 3.7% exactly), in which case the printed "280B" is missing a digit. As printed, the figure is internally inconsistent and the reader cannot determine which quantity is claimed.
evidence: Printed values: DeepSeek V4-Flash 4.6% = 13/284 = 4.577% ✓; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 4.8% = 6/125 = 4.80% ✓; GLM-5.3-Flash 5.6% = 18/320 = 5.625% ✓; Kimi K3 3.7% vs 104/280 = 37.14% ✗ (and 104/2800 = 3.71% ✓). The three other rows all reconcile to three significant figures, so the Kimi row is the sole outlier and the error is not a rounding-convention difference.
acceptance_test: Recompute all four fractions from the printed total/active pairs and confirm each equals the printed percentage to the printed precision. Resolve the Kimi row to a single unambiguous pair (either "2.8T/104B active" with 3.7%, or "280B/104B active" with 37.1%); if the latter, rescale the x-axis (max ≥ 40), redraw the bar, and update the title and caption (see FIG-A.1-02). The figure must not ship with a bar whose annotation and label disagree by 10×.

severity: P1 (major; the figure's title and caption assert a claim the figure's own data may falsify)
issue: The figure title asserts "Extreme sparsity: single-digit active (2026)" and the caption asserts "active fraction in single digits". If FIG-A.1-01 resolves to 37.1% for Kimi K3, both claims are false for one of the four surveyed families, and the appendix's opening thesis ("one that improves efficiency (more context, cheaper tokens) rather than raw capability", printed p. 432) rests on a pattern that one of the four models does not exhibit. The title is doing argumentative work, not merely labelling work, so it must be true of every plotted family.
evidence: Title: "Extreme sparsity: single-digit active (2026)". Caption: "four open models, total vs activated parameters, and active fraction in single digits — fractions are [DERIVED] from the 1P model-card counts". Plotted values: 4.6%, 3.7% (or 37.1%), 4.8%, 5.6%.
acceptance_test: After FIG-A.1-01 is resolved, re-derive the title and caption claim from the four plotted values. If any family is ≥10% active, restate the title and caption to the actual range (e.g. "active fractions: 4.6%–37%") and revise the A.1 opening paragraph so the thesis is not contradicted by the figure two paragraphs below it.

figure: FIGURE A.2 — Vendor-reported ratios: % remaining (appears twice, under the same figure number)
severity: P1 (major; production defect — one figure number, two different renderings, two consecutive pages)
issue: FIGURE A.2 is printed twice, on consecutive pages, under the same number, with materially different visual treatments and different footnote text. The p. 438 rendering is monochrome (black model names, black arrows, red warning box) with the footnote "*Metric scopes differ. x% remaining = (100 − x)% reduction, per every row." The p. 439 rendering is colour-coded (red/blue/green model names and matching arrows) with the footnote "*Metric scopes differ. 7% remaining = 93% reduction." The two captions are near-duplicates with slightly different wording. This is a duplicate figure, not a legitimate cross-reference, and it also breaks the book's visual language (the same figure is monochrome on one page and colour-coded on the next).
evidence: p. 438: "FIGURE A.2: Vendor-relative KV/compute ratios. Vendor-reported percentages remaining relative to each model's own reference, not a shared baseline. Every row states its metric scope in figure: ..." with footnote "x% remaining = (100 − x)% reduction, per every row." p. 439: "FIGURE A.2: Vendor-relative KV/compute ratios. Vendor-reported percentages remaining relative to each model's own reference, not a shared baseline. Every row states its metric scope in figure: ..." with footnote "7% remaining = 93% reduction." Row data are identical in both (V4-Flash 100%→~7% / ~10%; V4-Pro 100%→~10% / ~27%; GLM-5.3-Flash 100%→~23% / ~33%).
acceptance_test: Exactly one FIGURE A.2 exists in the built PDF. Verify by searching the PDF for the string "FIGURE A.2" and confirming a single occurrence, and by confirming the surviving rendering carries one footnote (recommend the general form "x% remaining = (100 − x)% reduction, per every row", which covers all five rows, rather than the single-row exemplar). If the colour-coded version is retained, add a one-line legend or drop the per-row colour, since the colour currently encodes nothing the reader is told about.

severity: P2 (major; the figure and its own caption state different validation thresholds)
issue: The green arrow from box 2 to box 3 is labelled "validate vs 800 ms target", but the caption states that the validate step compares measured TTFT p99 against "the hypothesis criterion (TTFT p99 < 300 ms, §8 Step 3) under the capstone's 8.80 ms TTFT target (§8 Step 0)". Three different thresholds are in play (800 ms in the drawing, 300 ms criterion in the caption, 8.80 ms target in the caption) and the reader cannot tell which one governs the loop. The figure also prints a baseline of "TTFT p99 ~450 ms" in box 1, which already exceeds the caption's 300 ms criterion — so under the caption's reading the loop fails at step one, while under the figure's 800 ms reading it passes. The diagram's central causal claim (assumption → derived → pattern → feedback) is therefore not determinable from the page.
evidence: Figure box 1: "baseline TTFT p99 ~450 ms". Arrow label: "validate vs 800 ms target". Caption: "the validate step compares the load test's measured TTFT p99 against the hypothesis criterion (TTFT p99 < 300 ms, §8 Step 3) under the capstone's 8.80 ms TTFT target (§8 Step 0)."
acceptance_test: One threshold governs the validate step. Label the arrow with the criterion actually applied (e.g. "validate: TTFT p99 < 300 ms (§8 Step 3)") and make the caption name the same quantity and value; if the 800 ms figure is a different quantity (e.g. an end-to-end budget rather than TTFT), name it explicitly in both places. Cross-check that the box-1 baseline and the criterion are on the same metric and the same units, and that the mini-case on printed p. 421 uses the same numbers.

figure: FIGURE 26.2 — box 1 vs prose on printed p. 421
severity: P2 (major; an unresolvable token in the prose that the figure is supposed to instantiate)
issue: The mini-case prose on printed p. 421 states "the host serves ~2.0 rps ceiling (the p near 1 behind box 1's inflated compute)". The token "the p near 1" is not defined anywhere in the visible text and has at least two readings: (a) a utilization ratio ρ ≈ 1, which would directly contradict the figure's box-1 "utilization ~45%"; (b) a p99 latency near 1 second, which would contradict the figure's "baseline TTFT p99 ~450 ms" and the arrow's "800 ms target". Because the figure is the visual form of this argument, an ambiguous parenthetical in the prose that contradicts either figure value is a substantive defect, not a typo.
evidence: Printed p. 421: "the host serves ~2.0 rps ceiling (the p near 1 behind box 1's inflated compute)". FIGURE 26.2 box 1: "request rate ~2 rps, utilization ~45%, baseline TTFT p99 ~450 ms". Arrow: "validate vs 800 ms target".
acceptance_test: Replace "the p near 1" with an explicit, defined quantity and symbol (e.g. "the p99 TTFT near 1 s" or "utilization ρ ≈ 1"), and confirm the value agrees with FIGURE 26.2 box 1 and with the arrow label. If the intended quantity is utilization, update the figure's "utilization ~45%"; if it is latency, update the baseline and the validate threshold.

figure: FIGURE A.3 — conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
severity: P2 (major; a legend declares a visual encoding the figure does not implement)
issue: The legend states "Model architecture (dashed) — foundation, efficiency, MoE; darker shade = MoE". The three architecture bands (Transformer ~2017, Efficient Transformer ~2020, MoE Transformer ~2022) are rendered in the same brown fill, so the "darker shade = MoE" cue is not present in the drawing. A reader who trusts the legend will look for a shade distinction that does not exist, and the MoE band is not visually distinguished from the two non-MoE architecture bands by anything except its text label.
evidence: Legend row 1: "Model architecture (dashed) — foundation, efficiency, MoE; darker shade = MoE". Bands: "Transformer –2017", "Efficient Transformer –2020", "MoE Transformer –2022" all appear in an identical mid-brown fill with dashed outlines.
acceptance_test: Either darken the MoE Transformer band (and only that band) so the legend's cue is literally true, or delete the "darker shade = MoE" clause from the legend. Verify by rendering the page in grayscale and confirming the MoE band is separable from the other two architecture bands by tone alone.

figure: FIGURE A.3 — legend swatch for the "Fleet (thick)" category
severity: P3 (minor; legend swatch does not demonstrate the encoding it names)
issue: The legend's third swatch is a thin purple square labelled "Fleet (thick) — multi-model 'intelligence placement'", but the swatch itself is not thick; the thickness encoding that distinguishes the Agent Fleet band is visible only in the drawing, not in the key. A reader decoding the legend cannot infer what "thick" means from the key.
evidence: Legend row 3: a narrow purple square, same height as the other two swatches, followed by "Fleet (thick) — multi-model 'intelligence placement'". In the drawing, the "Agent Fleet –2026" band is visibly taller than the others.
acceptance_test: Render the Fleet legend swatch at the same vertical thickness as the Agent Fleet band (or add a second, thicker swatch), so the key demonstrates the encoding rather than naming it.

severity: P3 (minor; the figure's own sub-caption and the book caption describe different objects)
issue: The sub-caption under the drawing reads "Selected illustrative mechanism milestones — a non-comprehensive chronology: approximate era markers (≈), not release dates", while the book caption reads "A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems ... the vertical stacking is a layering (which capabilities sit on which substrate), not a causal lineage". The first calls the object a chronology, the second explicitly disclaims chronology. The caption's disclaimer is the correct framing, but the sub-caption still tells the reader the figure is a chronology.
evidence: Sub-caption: "Selected illustrative mechanism milestones — a non-comprehensive chronology: approximate era markers (≈), not release dates. [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]". Caption: "The dates are approximate era markers, not a rigorously established chronology, and the vertical stacking is a layering ... not a causal lineage".
acceptance_test: Rewrite the sub-caption to match the caption's framing (e.g. "Selected illustrative mechanism milestones — a non-comprehensive layering, not a chronology: approximate era markers (≈), not release dates"), so that no text on the page calls the figure a chronology.

figure: FIGURE A.4 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
severity: P3 (minor; inconsistent treatment of the chapter-reference column)
issue: Every band carries a chapter reference except "Inside post-training (build-time)", which has none. The reader cannot tell whether post-training is deliberately excluded (because it is build-time rather than serving-time) or whether the reference was simply omitted. Given that the figure's purpose is to route the reader to the relevant chapters, an empty cell is a navigational gap.
evidence: Right-hand references: "Ch18, Ch20"; "Ch17-20, Ch24"; "Ch19, Ch24"; "Ch22"; [blank for post-training]; "Ch10"; "Ch7, Ch8"; "Ch3, Ch8".
acceptance_test: Either supply the chapter reference(s) for post-training or replace the blank with an explicit marker (e.g. "build-time; see Ch. 5") consistent with the figure's own "(build-time)" qualifier. No band may be left with an unexplained empty reference cell.

severity: P3 (minor; notation inconsistency in a navigational element)
issue: The reference column mixes a range shorthand with comma lists: "Ch17-20, Ch24" versus "Ch18, Ch20", "Ch19, Ch24", "Ch7, Ch8", "Ch3, Ch8". A reader cannot tell whether "Ch17-20" means Ch. 17 through Ch. 20 inclusive or something else, and the mixed style makes the column harder to scan.
evidence: "Inside agent runtime — Ch17-20, Ch24" against "Across a fleet of models — Ch18, Ch20" and "Inside attention — Ch7, Ch8".
acceptance_test: Use one notation throughout the column (e.g. "Ch. 17–20, Ch. 24" with an en dash and a period after "Ch", matching the book's house style elsewhere), and confirm the range's endpoints are the intended chapters.

figure: FIGURE A.4 — colour encoding and grayscale behaviour
severity: P3 (minor; hue-only encoding in the light bands)
issue: The note under the figure states "blue = system-side; green = model-side; darker = more intelligence". Within the system group the two lightest bands ("Inside post-training (build-time)" and "Inside test-time search") are both pale blue and both pale-ish, and the system/model split is carried by hue alone in those rows; in grayscale the blue and green families converge in the light end. The SYSTEM/MODEL axis labels on the left do carry the distinction, so the figure remains interpretable, but the hue cue is doing redundant work that fails in grayscale.
evidence: Bands: dark navy "Across a fleet of models"; mid blue "Inside agent runtime", "Inside tools"; pale blue "Inside test-time search", "Inside post-training (build-time)"; dark green "Inside MoE routing"; mid green "Inside attention"; pale green "Inside weights". Note: "blue = system-side; green = model-side; darker = more intelligence".
acceptance_test: Render the page in grayscale and confirm that every band can be assigned to SYSTEM or MODEL using the axis bracket alone; if any band becomes ambiguous, add a non-colour cue (e.g. a bracket or tick on the left axis spanning each group) rather than relying on hue.

severity: P3 (minor; malformed sentence and stray parenthesis in a caption that carries the figure's argument)
issue: The caption's chain sentence is malformed: "Chain: ASSUMPTION (box 1) holds assumed scenario inputs, not instrumented FACTs) → DERIVED → PATTERN;". There is an unmatched closing parenthesis after "FACTs)" and the sentence has no verb connecting "Chain:" to the parenthetical. The caption is the only place the reader learns what the three boxes' labels mean in the book's evidence taxonomy, so a broken sentence here is costly.
evidence: Caption text as printed: "Chain: ASSUMPTION (box 1) holds assumed scenario inputs, not instrumented FACTs) → DERIVED → PATTERN; the validate step compares ..."
acceptance_test: Repair to a single well-formed sentence, e.g. "Chain: ASSUMPTION (box 1 — assumed scenario inputs, not instrumented FACTs) → DERIVED → PATTERN;", and confirm parentheses balance across the full caption.

severity: P3 (minor; probable typo in the metric name that the figure's own labels depend on)
issue: The prose on printed p. 421 reads "the figures below are expressed as TTFT 999 on that host", where the figure and the surrounding text use "TTFT p99" (box 1: "baseline TTFT p99 ~450 ms"). "TTFT 999" is not a metric defined anywhere in the book and is almost certainly a corrupted "TTFT p99". Because this sentence is the one that tells the reader how to read the figure's latency numbers, the corruption is worth fixing rather than leaving to the reader.
evidence: Printed p. 421: "the figures below are expressed as TTFT 999 on that host (the sub-second latencies are time-to-first-token, not end-to-end)". FIGURE 26.2 box 1: "baseline TTFT p99 ~450 ms".
acceptance_test: Confirm against the manuscript source whether the string is "TTFT p99"; if so, correct the rendered text, and confirm the metric name matches the book's defined vocabulary (TTFT / TPOT / ITL) used elsewhere.
